pr.title: perf: compact coalesced range storage
pr.body:
`IPAddressRange.coalescing` currently allocates a second array with input-sized capacity, including when the result collapses to very few ranges. Compact the sorted buffer in place, return that buffer when every range survives, and copy reduced output into fresh storage when ranges merge.

The comparator, exact coverage, endpoint handling, generic Sequence API and caller-owned values are preserved. Add focused tests for single-pass input, aliasing, boundary cases, disjoint/collapsed shapes and sparse merges. Preserve both the rejected initial experiment and accepted compact-storage evidence without rewriting historical observations.

Existing qualification: matched Swift 6.4.2 suites and CLI benchmarks on macOS, native ARM64 Linux and x86-64 Linux, plus Swift 6.2.4 ARM64 compatibility; 5,220 test executions and 231 CLI differential comparisons passed. The accepted candidate reduced macOS range-derived RSS by 27.15% in that experiment and avoided the initial candidate’s Linux memory regressions. The roughly 2–3% x86-64 sparse-merge CPU cost remains an accepted, documented tradeoff; these are workload-specific historical results.

Fresh validation against current main is underway. Merge is gated on passing CI and integration checks. A new upstream release and an explicit cidrmerge dependency update, tests and matched benchmarks will follow separately. cidrmerge PR #25 preserved reports only; this PR supplies the missing upstream implementation integration.

head_commit.message:
perf: compact coalesced range storage

Reuse the sorted buffer when every input range survives. Compact the sorted prefix in place and copy merged output into fresh storage so heavily collapsed results do not retain input-sized capacity.

Preserve ordering, exact coverage, the generic Sequence API and caller-owned input values. Add single-pass, aliasing, boundary and sparse-merge coverage, and retain both prototype reports.

Validation: matched Swift 6.4.2 suites and CLI benchmarks on macOS, ARM64 Linux and x86-64 Linux; Swift 6.2.4 ARM64 compatibility suites. All 5,220 test executions and 231 CLI differential comparisons passed. The measured x86 sparse-merge CPU tradeoff is accepted and documented.
